column2: Factual Passages: A collection of facts with a detailed, sequential description of a specific topic
Discursive Passages: Opinion/argument-based passages that require reasoning and logic

column3: Focus: Viewpoints, arguments, conclusions (not just facts)
Note: Ideas may feel random or loosely connected—understand the overall message

column1: How to Approach Them for Answering

column2: Questions First Strategy: Read the questions before reading the passage (most passages)

column3: Why: Helps you spot keywords/data and find answers faster

column2: Handling Discursive Content: Read the full passage to understand the author’s viewpoint

column3: Look for: Main idea, tone, viewpoint, and a suitable title

column2: Navigating MCQs: Read every option carefully

column3: Tip: Options can be very similar—avoid rushing
If unsure: Use elimination to remove clearly wrong choices first

column2: Tackling Vocabulary Questions: Replace the target word in the sentence with the options

column3: Pick: The option that fits best without changing the meaning
Improve vocabulary: Daily reading + write new words in a notebook

column2: Writing Direct Answers: Keep answers concise and to the point

column3: Use: Your own words where possible
Stay relevant: Answer only what is asked

column2: Verification: Double-check the question after finding an answer

column3: Factual passages: Answers usually follow the same order as the questions
